title: Nirdosha Guard Data Sources v1
description: Environment-bound logical data-source manifest for the guard runtime. It contains references to environment variables, never secret values.

schema.description: Manifest schema identifier used by the guard loader.

application.description: Application or deployment identity that owns these bindings.

generated_from_env.description: Proves that endpoint and credential values are resolved from the container environment, not committed to source.

environment_namespace.description: Prefix used to namespace environment variables for this deployment.

generated_at.description: Generation timestamp for diagnostics; it is not a trust timestamp.

environment_revision.description: Deployment or orchestrator revision that supplied the environment.

manifest_hash.description: SHA-256 of the canonical manifest after removing this field; used to bind guard startup to exact configuration.

id.description: Logical source identifier referenced by datasets and guard policies, such as `PG`, `K`, or `IDP`.

kind.description: Logical data-store class; this is the policy and lineage vocabulary, not a network protocol.

driver.description: Concrete access driver selected by the guard/runtime implementation.

url_env.description: Environment variable containing the endpoint or connection URL. The value is resolved at startup and is never written to this manifest.

credential_env.description: Optional environment variable containing a credential, token, or password; it must not be logged or persisted.

region_env.description: Optional environment variable containing an object-store or cloud region.

namespace.description: Logical namespace, database, bucket, topic prefix, or filesystem root used within the endpoint.

access.description: Maximum access mode the guard runtime may request from this source.

tls_required.description: When true, startup rejects a resolved endpoint that is not TLS-protected where the driver supports TLS.

healthcheck.description: Named non-destructive health-check operation the driver must perform before admitting the source.

connect_timeout_ms.description: Bounded connection/health-check timeout in milliseconds; it is not a solver determinism control.

pool_max.description: Maximum connection or client pool size for drivers that support pooling.

required.description: Whether application startup fails closed when this source is absent or unhealthy.

lineage_label.description: Stable label emitted in lineage and audit evidence without exposing the resolved URL.

additionalProperties.description: Non-secret driver metadata used for diagnostics or capability negotiation.

metadata.description: Additional non-secret metadata; secrets and resolved URLs are forbidden here.

hash.description: Lowercase SHA-256 digest formatted as `sha256:<64 hex characters>`.
